dm_01: How to run the fifteen-minute intake review. This is the most important thing you will do on a firm call — the live demo. Watch the beats, watch where you pause, and watch the two or three lines you must say word for word. This is internal. It is coaching, not the customer script.
dm_02: Before you open the laptop, set the frame. Name their pain in their words: the ninety-minute cold read, the client who re-tells the story three times, the shoebox of pay stubs someone has to reconstruct. Get them nodding first. You are not selling software yet — you are naming a problem they feel every week.
dm_03: Open on the worker's home — not the firm side. Say it plainly: this record belongs to the worker, not to us and not to you. That one sentence is the whole company. It is why we are not a referral service and not just another intake tool. Let it land before you click anything.
dm_04: Show records going in. Drag in pay stubs, texts, screenshots — no sorting, no folders. Say: the worker never organizes this; the system infers the types. Tie it back to their pain — this is the shoebox, already sorted, before it ever reaches your desk.
dm_05: Now show how it reaches the firm — the worker enters your firm code and chooses to send it. Emphasize chooses. The worker decides who sees the record. That is not a compliance footnote — it is the legal foundation that keeps this clean. Say it on every demo.
dm_06: Switch to the firm queue. The intake arrives already organized — records counted, timeline rebuilt, gaps flagged. Pause here and let them feel the contrast with the ninety-minute cold read you named at the top. Do not narrate every field. Let the silence do the work.
dm_07: The decision card. This is the money shot — slow all the way down. It is the ten-second read: what is on file, the sequence, the key dates. Say: this is what replaces the first hour of every intake. Then stop talking and let them scan it.
dm_08: Claim Lens. Elements on file, and the gaps that remain. Here you land the metric we own — Coverage Rate — the percentage of the statutory elements that actually have material on file. Say the name out loud. It is the number Eve and Clio cannot compute, because they do not organize the worker's own record.
dm_09: The source link. Click one fact — and its exact source page opens right beside it. This is the trust moment; do it live, do it slowly. Say: verify in one click, not twenty minutes. Every fact traces to its page. This is what earns an attorney's trust, and it is the one thing every rival is missing.
dm_10: The actions. Accept, request more, or decline — one click each. Keep this quick. The point is simply that the decision stays with the attorney. We never make it for them. Say that: the software organizes, the lawyer decides. Then move on.
dm_11: Now the guardrail — the lines you must never cross, even when a firm pushes you. Never say the worker has a good case. Never say a case is worth a number. Never promise an outcome. If they ask does it score the case — the answer is no, and that is the point. We describe the record; we never characterize the case. Say it with confidence — that discipline is the product.
dm_12: Reframe every strength through Coverage Rate. When they ask what makes you different, do not list features. Say: we measure how complete the worker's record is against what the law requires, we link every fact to its source, and the worker chooses who sees it. Completeness and provenance — never a verdict. That is the whole pitch in one breath.
dm_13: The close. Ask for one specific thing: a firm code, or a seat in the pilot. Say — get a firm code where workers are already organizing intakes for two-minute attorney decisions. Then stop. After you ask, go silent. Whoever speaks first loses. Let them answer.
dm_14: The beats, timed. Two minutes naming the pain. Six minutes on the worker record and the firm binder. Three minutes on Coverage Rate and the source link — that is the heart. Two minutes on the guardrail and the difference. Two minutes to ask and go quiet. Fifteen total. Run it the same way every time until it is muscle memory.
dm_15: One last thing. The reason this demo works is that it is honest. We are not claiming to be flawless — we use A I too. We are claiming something better: every fact is reviewable, the source is one click away, and the worker owns and chooses. Sell the discipline, not the magic. Now go run it.
